concepts.cell: consumer-device firmware or hardware x researchers or science
concepts.title: Detect silent wearable firmware changes that threaten studies
concepts.text: Diffs successive firmware images and companion-app packages of a fitness wearable, flags changed step, sleep and heart-rate algorithms, and writes a dated data-validity memo for research teams whose cohort data spans those versions.
concepts.pitch: For research groups and graduate students who collect activity data on consumer wearables and cannot tell when a vendor update quietly changed the metric. It unpacks two or more versions of a device's firmware and companion app, locates the signal-processing code that changed, and reports which date ranges in a dataset are not comparable. Nobody does this because scientists treat the device as a black box and hackers have no research customer.

concepts.cell: consumer-device firmware or hardware x researchers or science
concepts.title: Bluetooth kitchen scale becomes a beehive weight logger
concepts.text: Reverse-engineers the Bluetooth protocol of a retail kitchen scale from captured notifications, then builds a calibrated logger that streams weight and battery level to CSV with drift correction for bee-research field trials.
concepts.pitch: For beekeepers, ecology students and small labs that need continuous mass data for hives, nests or soil trays but cannot afford a $300 research logger. A $12 retail scale is enumerated over Bluetooth, its weight packets are decoded, and the output is calibrated against reference masses with a drift curve and a protocol note others can reuse. Nobody has done it because the people who crack gadget protocols build apps for themselves and scientists don't open the case.

concepts.cell: consumer-device firmware or hardware x researchers or science
concepts.title: Score agents on reverse-engineering real retail firmware
concepts.text: Builds a benchmark from open-source smart-plug and e-reader firmware, stripped and rebuilt with planted quirks, then scores how far an autonomous agent recovers the protocol, file formats and hidden behavior in emulation.
concepts.pitch: For AI-capability and safety researchers who need hard, realistic, gradable autonomy tests that aren't synthetic puzzles. Open-source consumer firmware (Tasmota and ESPHome plugs, open e-reader and wearable images) is rebuilt with planted, documented quirks so ground truth is known, then handed to an agent in a sandbox with an emulator and tools. Nobody has built it because retail firmware work lives in hobbyist forums, far from eval labs, and real devices make grading impossible.

concepts.cell: extract and structure x a codebase
concepts.title: Tabulate every environment variable a repository reads
concepts.text: Scans a repository's source, Dockerfiles and CI files for every environment variable and setting it reads, then writes a table of name, default, type, required status, readers and file locations, plus an example config.
concepts.pitch: For developers inheriting or open-sourcing a service with no config documentation, and for the person who must deploy it on a Friday. One pass across languages and deploy files produces a deduplicated census, flags variables read with conflicting defaults, and drafts the example env file. People ask for a README; nobody asks for the underlying table, which is the thing that actually gets used.

concepts.cell: extract and structure x a codebase
concepts.title: Lift hardcoded game balance numbers into editable spreadsheets
concepts.text: Pulls every hardcoded enemy stat, item price, drop rate and spawn rule out of a game mod's scripts into a spreadsheet with source locations, so designers can tune balance in one place.
concepts.pitch: For modders and small game teams whose balance lives as magic numbers scattered across hundreds of script files, so designers can't see or compare it. The tool turns the code into a flat table (entity, field, value, unit guess, file:line) and can write edits back to the exact locations. Designers have spreadsheets and the data is in code, and nobody has done the one-off lift because it is too tedious by hand.

concepts.cell: extract and structure x a codebase
concepts.title: Extract a cited fact database from a monorepo
concepts.text: Reads a polyglot monorepo's code, infrastructure and pipeline files to extract services, endpoints, tables, queues, jobs and their relations into a queryable database, each row citing file and line, then re-checks every citation.
concepts.pitch: For platform and architecture teams who need to answer 'what reads this table?' or 'what breaks if this queue goes down?' across a system nobody holds in their head. A fact base with verifiable evidence per row replaces stale architecture diagrams. Summaries of codebases exist, but a database where every row is independently re-verified against its cited lines, and diffable between two commits, has not been built.

concepts.cell: financial and legal paperwork x the public or a community
concepts.title: Open-books page for a hobby club
concepts.text: Turns a hobby club treasurer's bank export and receipt photos into a plain-language open-books page for members, reconciling every line, flagging unmatched spending, and publishing a one-page yearly report.
concepts.pitch: For volunteer treasurers of clubs, leagues, game guilds and open-source projects who collect dues from dozens of members and answer 'where did the money go?' by hand. The treasurer drops in the bank CSV and a folder of receipt photos, and gets a reconciled ledger plus a members' page with categories, totals and a short list of items needing explanation. Nobody does it because community money sits in a gap between personal bookkeeping tools and formal nonprofit accounting software.

concepts.cell: financial and legal paperwork x the public or a community
concepts.title: Neighbors' lease clauses compared side by side
concepts.text: Compares redacted leases that tenants of one landlord voluntarily upload, aligns clauses across copies, and publishes a shared map showing which fees and terms differ between neighbors for the same unit type.
concepts.pitch: For tenant associations and building groups where each renter signed a nominally identical lease and none can tell whether they got the same terms. Members upload their own redacted lease, the system aligns clause by clause, and the group sees a diff map: this late fee is 5 percent for most units and 10 percent for yours, this renewal clause appears in only seven leases. Individuals only ever see their own copy, so the comparison, which needs many contracts at once, has been out of reach.

concepts.cell: financial and legal paperwork x the public or a community
concepts.title: County form guide built from neighbors' filings
concepts.text: Turns neighbors' redacted, completed permit and benefit forms plus their outcomes into a shared field-by-field guide for one county, walking newcomers through each form and updating when the agency revises it.
concepts.pitch: For immigrant networks, mutual-aid groups and neighborhood associations that already pass 'how I filled it in' knowledge by word of mouth. Volunteers contribute redacted completed forms with notes on what was accepted or bounced, and the system builds a living guide per form: what each box really wants, common rejection causes, and where to get help, with a clear 'this is information, not legal advice' referral. A watcher detects when the agency publishes a new form version and flags the guide as stale. No one has done it because each filing is private and one-off, so the community's collective experience was never turned into a shared reference.

concepts.cell: reverse-engineer or unlock x a business or its customers
concepts.title: Rescue data from abandoned accounting software
concepts.text: Decodes an abandoned accounting program's proprietary data files by comparing byte patterns against on-screen records, then exports customers, invoices and balances to CSV and SQLite with a documented parser a small business can keep.
concepts.pitch: For a small business whose bookkeeping software vendor has vanished, leaving years of records in an unreadable file format and no export button. The user supplies the data folder and a few screenshots of known records. The structure is inferred, checked against those records, and turned into a reusable parser. Nobody has done this because each such job is too small for a reverse-engineering consultant to take on.

concepts.cell: reverse-engineer or unlock x a business or its customers
concepts.title: Label printer driver from a phone Bluetooth log
concepts.text: Decodes a Bluetooth log captured from a vendor's phone app to reconstruct a shop label printer's undocumented protocol, then writes a laptop driver that prints inventory labels directly from a spreadsheet.
concepts.pitch: For a shop owner locked into a cheap label printer whose phone app can only print one label at a time. The owner turns on the phone's built-in Bluetooth snoop log, prints a few test labels, and hands over the file. The protocol is worked out from the packets, and a PC tool prints in bulk. Nobody does it because the wins are tiny per device, yet there are thousands of such devices.

concepts.cell: reverse-engineer or unlock x a business or its customers
concepts.title: Resurrect an orphaned booking app's dead server
concepts.text: Captures traffic between a salon's orphaned booking client and its dead vendor server, infers the message formats, and reimplements a drop-in server so the paid software keeps syncing appointments on current Windows.
concepts.pitch: For businesses that bought a licensed desktop and phone booking system, then watched the vendor shut down its cloud, leaving the software unusable. The owner's own client runs against a local replacement server, rebuilt from recorded traffic, local certificates and the client's binary. It restores something the owner already paid for. It has not been done because the work is unglamorous and the vendors are gone, so there is no one to ask.

concepts.cell: coordinate many agents x family or household
concepts.title: Per-member agents negotiate the household's weekly schedule
concepts.text: Assigns one scheduling agent to each household member, who negotiate the week's school runs, dinners, chores and appointments from imported calendars and stated limits, then output a shared plan with flagged conflicts.
concepts.pitch: For busy households where one parent is the unpaid scheduler. Each member imports a calendar and fills a short form of must-haves and nice-to-haves, and their agent bargains with the others, so the plan shows who gave ground and which clashes only humans can resolve. Nobody has tried it because multi-agent work targets developers and family tools use one assistant that treats the household as one blob.

concepts.cell: coordinate many agents x family or household
concepts.title: Reconcile relatives' conflicting memories into one family recipe
concepts.text: Interviews each relative separately about a grandmother's signature dish, then has a mediator agent reconcile their conflicting memories into one recipe card that marks disputed steps and lists a cook-off test plan.
concepts.pitch: For families trying to save a dish nobody wrote down. Each relative talks to their own interviewer agent by phone voice note or text, and a mediator compares the versions, finds where they agree, and turns the disagreements (lard or butter, how long to rest the dough) into a small cook-off test. Nobody has done it because it needs one agent per witness plus a reconciler, and the people who cook for family don't usually think of multi-agent setups.

concepts.cell: coordinate many agents x family or household
concepts.title: Sibling agents negotiate a fair eldercare rota across households
concepts.text: Runs a standing agent for each sibling and one for a parent's written wishes, negotiating a fair monthly visit, errand and appointment rota across households, tracking a fairness ledger and escalating deadlocks to humans.
concepts.pitch: For siblings splitting a parent's care from different cities, where resentment about who does more is often the real problem. Each sibling's agent holds their stated availability and limits, a parent agent holds the parent's own written preferences and has first say on what they accept, and a shared ledger tracks visits, drives and money over months, so fairness is visible instead of argued. Nobody has built it because it needs persistent multi-party agents with real calendar access and consent from everyone, which neither developer tools nor consumer family apps provide.

concepts.cell: investigate a question x consumer-device firmware or hardware
concepts.title: Overnight battery drain traced by controlled experiments
concepts.text: Runs controlled overnight experiments on an Android phone over adb, toggling radios, sync and app standby buckets while logging battery stats, then ranks which setting explains the unexplained drain.
concepts.pitch: For anyone whose phone loses 15 percent overnight and who is tired of forum folklore. An experiment loop plans a test matrix, runs one night per condition, and reports effect sizes with confidence. Nobody does this because a single night is noisy and the bookkeeping across nights is tedious, and the loop does the bookkeeping.

concepts.cell: investigate a question x consumer-device firmware or hardware
concepts.title: Release notes versus firmware binaries across five years
concepts.text: Downloads every public firmware release of a consumer gadget line, unpacks and diffs them, and tabulates what silently changed in endpoints, permissions, ciphers and features against what the release notes claimed.
concepts.pitch: For privacy researchers, consumer journalists and owners deciding whether to update. It treats a product's update history as a dataset and asks what the vendor changed that it never said. Nobody does this at scale because unpacking, diffing and reading dozens of images per product is weeks of grind.

concepts.cell: investigate a question x consumer-device firmware or hardware
concepts.title: Cloud shutdown drill for every gadget at home
concepts.text: Sinkholes each household gadget's vendor domains one at a time from a laptop hotspot, tests which features survive, and produces a ranked map of what bricks if the cloud disappears.
concepts.pitch: For smart-home owners and repair advocates who worry about the next vendor shutdown. A drill harness plans which domains to block, drives each device's features through its app or local interface, and records what keeps working offline. Nobody has made this systematic because testing one device takes an afternoon and finding the critical domain is guesswork.

prior_art.what: env-audit: multi-language scan (Python, Node, Go, Rust, Ruby, Shell, Docker) producing a documented .env.example with defaults, required/optional, sensitive flags, file locations, JSON output and a CI --check mode. Lacks CI-file scanning and conflicting-default flagging as far as seen.

envsniff (github.com/envsniff/envsniff): scans source for os.getenv/process.env/os.Getenv across languages, detects undocumented vars, generates .env.example, table/JSON/Markdown output, pre-commit and GitHub Action, optional AI-written descriptions.

Browser-based design and print tool for Phomemo label printers with no vendor app. README lists CSV import, variable templates, preview grid and batch printing. This is the PC bulk-from-spreadsheet outcome, delivered as a finished tool.

CUPS driver for Phomemo label and receipt printers. README says the protocol was reverse-engineered by sniffing the vendor app's traffic, and an issue thread covers further reverse engineering of newer models. HN discussion exists at news.ycombinator.com/item?id=45729340.

code-graph MCP: static scan of a polyglot (Laravel/React/NestJS/Go/Python) codebase into a Kuzu graph of files, HTTP routes, DB tables, queues. Edges store source_file, line and raw snippet, with a read/write/unknown mode and a confidence score. Answers 'what code touches table X'. Does not independently re-verify citations and has no commit diff; it is snapshot-only and needs a re-scan. Extraction is tree-sitter and regex, with AI only on the query side.

CodeRadius (HN Show HN 48830828, coderadius.ai): open-source tool that builds a queryable architecture graph (services, APIs, queues, databases, across repos and monorepos) from tree-sitter AST plus LLM extraction (Ollama or BYO key). Every node and edge carries grounding (source, evidence, 5-tier quality), it exposes the graph over MCP to Claude Code, Cursor and other agents, and 'cr blast' diffs a change against the graph. Now in maintenance mode, 23 stars. Missing: no stated step that independently re-verifies each row against its cited file and line, and evidence is extractor/LLM-call metadata rather than file:line quotes as far as I could see. Its diff is a PR blast radius against the graph, not a diff of two full fact bases.

Shoulder, a Devpost hackathon project. Each family member gets an agent on Claude Sonnet 4.5 (Bedrock, Strands Agents SDK) that negotiates caregiving duties, weighing tasks, capacities and fairness. It is open source (MIT). I could not open the page directly (403 or JS shell), so this comes from search-result summaries. I could not confirm a separate parent-wishes agent, a months-long fairness ledger, real calendar access or escalation to humans. A builder note says the arithmetic was kept outside the model to stop allocations drifting.

SRE-Bench (vals.ai, arXiv 2608.11469): 19 private from-scratch programs, 262 instances, 1,572 deterministically graded tasks. Covers network protocols, firmware (RevFirmware domain, 6 instances), file-format recovery, malware, with symbol-stripping variants. Differs from the concept: synthetic from-scratch code, not open-source retail firmware rebuilt with planted quirks, and no emulator-in-sandbox focus.

envdoc: deterministic CLI that finds every env var read in JS/TS, Python, Go and Ruby. It writes .env.example, prints a Markdown table and fails CI on undocumented vars. Misses Dockerfile and CI readers, defaults, required status and conflicting-default flags. README says 'no AI'.

Production write-up of a 46-repo knowledge graph in BigQuery. tree-sitter extraction plus Gemini for dynamic field access. Boundary edges for API endpoints, events, and DB tables (READS_FROM/WRITES_TO). Verification is a daily connection-rate metric, not per-row citation checks. No file/line evidence described and no commit diff.
PTO Today Finance Manager: phone receipt photo upload, click-to-match bank reconciliation, board/audit reports, $139/yr. Lacks a members' public page and AI; made for school PTOs, not hobby clubs.

Non-expert used ChatGPT/an LLM to reverse engineer a BLE cat printer from phone-side captured traffic (Apple PacketLogger, not Android snoop log) and build an image print pipeline. Partial driver; no bulk or spreadsheet printing, no shop use case.

Python library with CLI and GUI for NIIMBOT label printers over Bluetooth. Gives a PC print path with quantity and density settings and replaces the phone app. Related NIIMBOT projects: MultiMote/niimblue (820 stars), niimbluelib, niimprint, hass-niimbot.

wire-pod: community-built replacement server for the Anki/DDL Vector robot after the vendor's cloud went down; lets owners' existing devices keep working against a local server. Same method and outcome, consumer robot not business software, hand-built.

MoneyMinder: club/booster accounting with bank import (12,000+ banks), reconciliation, receipt storage, member statements, reports, $299/yr. Member-facing open-books page and receipt-to-line matching not confirmed.
TeddyCloud: open-source server replacement for the Boxine cloud used by the Toniebox, built by reverse engineering the device protocol.
HN comment: author reverse engineered the OUYA API after its servers shut down in 2019 and built a documented re-implementation so consoles work again.

IoTrimmer (Mandalari, Kolcun, Haddadi, Dubois, Choffnes): research framework that tests which destinations a consumer IoT device contacts and blocks those not needed for functionality. Same mechanism (per-destination blocking, check function survives) but aimed at privacy, not a ranked 'what bricks' map; no public code found.

Wii Balance Board read over Bluetooth by a Raspberry Pi. A comment (Graham Toal) reports using one as a beehive scale, with a relay pressing the sync button, plus temperature, humidity, pressure and sound sensors. Consumer Bluetooth scale reused as a hive scale, but no kitchen scale, no new protocol reverse-engineering, no CSV or drift curve.

SRE-Bench (Spence et al.): contamination-free agentic reverse-engineering benchmark, 19 private expert-built programs, 262 binary instances, 1,572 deterministically graded tasks, tested on GPT and Claude models. Built from scratch with planted known ground truth and anti-analysis mechanisms. Targets general binaries (mentions firmware only as motivation). No retail firmware, no emulation, no smart-plug or e-reader.

CodeGraph: graph of service dependencies (direct API calls and message-queue relationships) for on-call debugging, queryable with Cypher. README mentions mapping specific functions and lines and versioned snapshots over time. Does not list tables as node types and does not mention citation re-verification.

Python library, CLI and server for the Phomemo M110 label printer, written largely by Claude Code. Protocol came from earlier human reverse-engineering projects, not a fresh capture. Loops labels over one BLE connection (the README's example prints A-1, A-2, A-3).
Brother PT-P300BT: Android Bluetooth snoop log captured, then a Python driver written. The search summary did not mention AI. I did not open the page.
PTIME/CALO (SRI): personal calendar agents negotiate conflicts with other users' agents via distributed constraint optimization; no family or household framing, no shared plan output

Human practice guide for reconstructing a lost family recipe: oral histories from several relatives, ranges, repeated test attempts, reaching agreement on a version. Same outcome done manually, no AI or tool (seen in search snippet, not opened).

Collins et al. 2019 Sensors, 'Version Reporting and Assessment Approaches for New and Updated Activity and Heart Rate Monitors'. It documents the exact problem: firmware and software updates change device performance, same-model devices on different versions are distinct, and Garmin Vivosmart HR had 14 versions in ~30 months. Its remedy is an empirical bench and treadmill re-validation protocol plus version reporting. It does no firmware diffing and has no tooling.

A Bluetooth kitchen scale (Nutridays KT630LB) decoded over GATT with an ESP32-C3 and ESPHome. This is the same technique, but it feeds Home Assistant and is not a calibrated logger or aimed at hives. Page seen only as a search result, not opened.

AgentRE-Bench (v3.1, Oct 2026): scores AI agents on recovering behavior and hidden details of unknown Linux ELF and Windows PE binaries, with deterministic versioned ground truth, tool-call budgets, and Claude, GPT, Grok and Gemini on the leaderboard. Binaries, not consumer firmware; static analysis only, no emulation.

omnispex (Show HN 44636440): tree-sitter dependency extraction into a graph, with AI used only for semantic links on top of statically verified structure. It answers 'what breaks if I change X' across repos. Marketing page only, early access, with no per-row citations and no re-verification step.

Open Collective: public transparent budget and ledger with receipts required per expense, used by open-source projects. Public by default, but it is a platform that holds the money, not a bank-CSV reconciler, and receipts are private.

Blog post: Claude Opus 4.5 in Zed (after ChatGPT deep research) reverse-engineered the proprietary .TC OBD-II diagnostic log format and built a CSV converter in about 2 hours for roughly $6. Validated by plausibility checks, not against on-screen records. Not accounting.

Android Runner (the search result listed the fork Bla/android-runner). A non-AI framework that automates repeated Android battery experiments from JSON configs, with a batterystats plugin and run hooks. It covers the experiment-loop and bookkeeping half of the concept, but has no overnight scope, no setting-toggle ranking and no AI.

Public, continuously updated Apple IPSW firmware diffs across many iOS/iPadOS/macOS releases (via the ipsw tool). It is the same method (unpack and diff every release) but is aimed at security researchers, covers Apple only, and does no comparison against release notes or any privacy tabulation.

Reverse-engineered Web Bluetooth parser for Perfect Company kitchen scales (24-bit counts to grams) with disassembly notes. The README has a history log with timestamps but no CSV export, no user calibration procedure, no drift correction and no hive use. Opened and checked.
CLI script that lists env vars used in a project and generates .env.example. Only a repo description was seen; the README was not retrievable.
envdoc: Go-only generator of Markdown/HTML/dotenv/JSON env var docs from config struct tags and comments (not a cross-language scan).
Harvey: upload many leases and summarize or compare key terms across the set. Same cross-lease clause alignment, but built for legal teams and portfolios, not pooled tenant uploads.

Blog post: Claude helped reverse-engineer Yamaha Y-Trac .CTRK binary telemetry files (no export in the official app), with a Python parser validated against the original library's output, plus a TypeScript port. Not accounting or business data.

PEMAND: persona-enriched LLM multi-agent negotiation for household decision-making (one agent per member plus a moderator, per search snippets). Simulates household travel and mobility decisions for research. It has no calendar import, no weekly plan, and no conflict flagging for parents.

Voice-recording AI archiver that transcribes relatives' recipe stories into structured recipe cards (opened README). Single-narrator capture; no multi-witness comparison, dispute marking or cook-off plan.

ARENA: Android Studio plugin that resets battery stats per iteration and runs R statistics (Kruskal-Wallis, ANOVA). Covers repeated runs plus analysis. Hardware-measurement oriented, and I did not confirm automatic settings toggling. Seen in search results only, not opened.

AI-written reports built on ipsw diffing of iOS releases. It uses AI to describe what changed between firmware builds, but is vulnerability-oriented, covers a single platform, and does not compare against release-note claims.

Paper 'Not all steps are equal: Changing algorithms in wearable trackers changes outcomes'. Documents the problem: vendors change tracker algorithms mid-study, and the paper warns researchers to watch for it. It gives no tool that diffs firmware or apps, and no memo.
Reverse engineering of the Etekcity ESN00 BLE kitchen scale protocol by sniffing app traffic with Wireshark and adb. Documents the packet structure. No bees and no AI.

Blog (seen only in search results, not opened). Reportedly suggests asking Claude Code to scan process.env / os.environ and produce a documented .env.example, and to find every direct process.env read before consolidating config. This is ad-hoc prompting, with no census table, conflicting-default flags or Docker/CI coverage.
Non-AI tool (2021) that parses balance values from Chivalry: Medieval Warfare vanilla/mod source files into a spreadsheet; only dumps a weapon stamina-drain matrix, no write-back, no file:line table.

Local-first AI agent (built with Claude Code and hledger): extracts transactions from PDF bank statements and receipt photos into a plain-text ledger and gives category reports. Single-user personal finance. No reconciliation feature, no member-facing page, no club focus.

Leases as Forms (academic): analysis of ~170,000 Philadelphia eviction-court leases; finds leases vary more between landlords than within them and flags unlawful terms. Court-record data, not tenant-contributed, no per-group diff map, not shown to use an AI assistant. Seen in search results only (publisher page redirected on fetch).

LeaseCheck: renters anonymously report rent, fees, landlords and safety; compiled into transparency reports. Crowdsourced and tenant-side, but structured reports, not clause-aligned lease uploads. Landing page only, scale unverified.

MAP (CHI EA 2025): multi-agent LLM system that resolves conflicts between several users' preferences and schedules in a shared setting. The abstract fetch only confirmed multi-user conflict resolution with user feedback. The household and schedule framing comes from a search snippet. No per-member agents and no weekly family plan.

CalBench: benchmark for multi-agent calendar scheduling where each agent manages a private calendar. It measures displacement cost, burden fairness and privacy leakage. I saw it only in search results and did not open it. Research benchmark, not for households and not a product.
Home OS (open source): agents per domain incl. Family Coordinator for carpool, activities and drive times; function-based agents, no negotiation described

Heirloom AI (open source, Gemini): turns recipe cards, voice recordings and cooking videos into structured recipe entries with confidence levels and 'speculative gaps' for family to verify. No multi-relative interviews, no reconciliation of conflicting versions, no cook-off plan.

CareCommons: free iPhone app for siblings sharing parent care; shared task board, care log, schedules; nudges to redistribute when tasks pile on one person. No negotiation, no parent agent, no ledger of drives/money, AI not mentioned.

Battery Historian: analyzes bugreports (wakelocks, timelines) and offers A/B comparison of two bugreports. Archived Dec 2022. It does not run experiments, so the human does the bookkeeping across nights.

Home Assistant IoT classes (cloud polling/push vs local polling/push): established practice that classifies each integration by cloud dependency. A declared label per integration, not an empirically tested drill.

Beehive honey-super weighing over BLE. It uses a bathroom scale's load cell with an HX711, an Arduino and an HM-10 module, read from a browser. Bee use and BLE are present, but there is no reverse-engineered retail scale protocol, no CSV, no calibration or drift work, and no AI.

CrackMeBench: agents reverse-engineer symbol-poor binaries generated from seeded C, Rust and Go templates, with executable oracles in a Docker sandbox, evaluated on GPT-5.5, Claude Opus 4.7 and Kimi K2. Synthetic crackmes, not firmware.

MalwareBench: obfuscated real malware, two graded deliverables (behavior analysis and extractor tested on held-out variants), across Windows, Linux, macOS and Android. Realistic and gradable, but malware rather than consumer firmware.

DeepWiki (Devin/Cognition): LLM-generated repo wikis and architecture diagrams with links to source files. It is prose and diagrams, not a queryable fact table, and does no re-verification or commit-to-commit diff.

Self-hosted-style AI receipt reading plus bank CSV import (as described by a web search summary of TaxHacker-like tools, with CompteQC using Claude Vision for receipts and bank CSV/OFX dedupe). Aimed at freelancers and small businesses. No members' page, no unmatched-spending flags for a group. This URL was seen in search results but not opened.
DenserAI: landlord and property-manager tool that compares lease terms across properties. Mechanism matches; audience is the landlord.

Borderwise: guided questionnaire that picks and fills immigration forms, with attorney review. Single-vendor, not crowdsourced from neighbors' filings, no outcome-based per-field guide or version-staleness watcher.
HN comment: Claude Code decompiled an .exe for a lab instrument that only gave PDF reports, reverse-engineered the raw data format, and wrote an analysis suite. Anecdote; not accounting.

Cimaware, a data recovery software maker, says it reverse engineers each new file format at binary level to build recovery tools (seen in search result snippet only). Human-driven and format-by-format, not a general tool for abandoned accounting packages.
Python server emulator for a mobile game, built by reverse engineering the client API for preservation. No AI mentioned, and it is a game rather than business software.

Achiote (npm / KyaniteLabs MCP server, for Claude Code and Codex): reconstructs a family food memory into structured clues, a research plan and a minimum-viable nostalgia cue, and suggests follow-up questions for relatives. Works from one person's memory; no per-relative interviewer agents, no reconciling of conflicting accounts, no test plan.
Caring Village: established care-circle app (siblings coordinate care, shared calendar, tasks); human-driven, no fairness ledger or agents. Seen in search results only.

Nothing Community thread 'Investigating Nothing OS CPU Idle Behavior - Wake Locks & Background Services'. Search snippet says a user used GPT-5 to investigate why the CPU does not reach deep idle and why the phone drains overnight. I could not read the body, so I don't know whether adb experiments or multi-night runs were involved. Likely an anecdote, not a controlled loop.

Fetches old and new binaries, runs Ghidriff diffs, then an LLM pipeline (OpenAI, Claude or Ollama) writes severity-rated reports. This is AI-assisted binary diffing, but for security patch diffing. It has no release-notes comparison, no multi-year corpus and no consumer-gadget focus.
Manual test of a hub's offline capabilities per device/feature. Human-run, one platform, no domain sinkholing, no ranking, no AI.
Anecdotal article: a person blocked internet on all smart devices and reported what still worked. Blanket block, manual, no per-domain drill, no AI.
DIY practice guide: block device internet at router/firewall, log contacted servers, check what still works. Manual, per device, no harness.
